q: The laboratory preparation of dinitrogen oxide involves the heating of _____.
e: Dinitrogen oxide is prepared in the laboratory by heating ammonium nitrate.

q: Dinitrogen oxide is collected by the _____ of hot water.
e: Dinitrogen oxide is insoluble in hot water, so it is collected by the downward displacement of hot water.

q: Dinitrogen oxide is a colourless gas with a _____ odour.
e: Dinitrogen oxide ($N_2O$) is characterised by a sweetish odour.

q: Dinitrogen oxide is soluble in cold water but _____ in hot water.
e: The solubility of dinitrogen oxide decreases in hot water, making it insoluble.

q: Dinitrogen oxide is readily decomposed above _____.
e: Dinitrogen oxide readily decomposes into nitrogen and oxygen at temperatures above 600℃.

q: Nitrogen oxide is prepared in the laboratory by the reaction of copper with _____ nitric acid.
e: Nitrogen oxide ($NO$) is produced when copper reacts with dilute nitric acid.

q: Nitrogen oxide is collected by the downward displacement of _____ water.
e: Nitrogen oxide is insoluble in water and is collected by the downward displacement of cold water.

q: Nitrogen oxide is a colourless, _____ gas.
e: Nitrogen oxide ($NO$) is a colourless and odourless gas.

q: Nitrogen oxide combines directly with chlorine in the presence of charcoal to form yellow _____ gas.
e: Nitrogen oxide reacts with chlorine to form yellow nitrosyl chloride ($NOCl$) gas.

q: A cold acidified solution of iron(II) sulphate reacts with nitrogen oxide to give a brown _____ complex.
e: Nitrogen oxide forms a brown nitroso iron(II) sulphate complex, which is a standard test for $NO$.

q: Nitrogen dioxide is prepared in the laboratory by the reaction of copper with _____ nitric acid.
e: Nitrogen dioxide ($NO_2$) is produced when copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid.

q: Nitrogen dioxide is collected by the _____ of air.
e: Nitrogen dioxide is denser than air and soluble in water, so it is collected by upward displacement of air.

q: Nitrogen dioxide is a reddish brown gas with a pungent and _____ smell.
e: Nitrogen dioxide has a characteristic pungent and irritating smell.

q: At -10℃, nitrogen dioxide exists as a solid, colourless dimer molecule called _____.
e: At low temperatures, $NO_2$ dimerises to form colourless dinitrogen tetroxide ($N_2O_4$).

q: Nitrogen dioxide dissolves in water to form a mixture of nitric acid and _____.
e: When $NO_2$ dissolves in water, it forms a mixture of nitric acid ($HNO_3$) and nitrous acid ($HNO_2$).

q: When nitrogen dioxide reacts with aqueous alkalis, the corresponding nitrates and _____ are formed.
e: Nitrogen dioxide reacts with alkalis to produce a mixture of nitrates and nitrites.

q: Dinitrogen oxide gas is also commonly known as _____.
e: Dinitrogen oxide ($N_2O$) is widely known as laughing gas and is used as an anaesthetic.

q: The most thermally stable hydride of nitrogen is _____.
e: Ammonia ($NH_3$) is the most thermally stable binary hydride of nitrogen.

q: Ammonia is manufactured on a large scale by the _____ process.
e: The Haber process is the industrial method for synthesising ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen.

q: In the Haber process, nitrogen and hydrogen gases are mixed together in the ratio of _____ by volume.
e: The stoichiometric ratio for the Haber process is 1 volume of nitrogen to 3 volumes of hydrogen.

q: In the Haber process, the gas mixture is passed over an _____ catalyst.
e: An iron catalyst is used to speed up the reaction in the Haber process.

q: In the Haber process, the reaction is carried out at a high pressure of about _____.
e: A high pressure of approximately 200 atm is applied to favour the forward reaction in the Haber process.

q: In the Haber process, the reaction is carried out at a moderately high temperature of _____.
e: The optimum temperature for the Haber process is around 450℃.

q: In the laboratory preparation of ammonia, an excess of slaked lime and _____ are mixed and heated.
e: Ammonia is prepared in the lab by heating a mixture of slaked lime ($Ca(OH)_2$) and ammonium chloride.

q: Ammonia gas is dried by passage through a drying tower which contains the drying agent _____.
e: Quicklime ($CaO$) is used to dry ammonia gas because it does not react with it.

q: Since ammonia is lighter than air and very soluble in water, it is collected by the _____.
e: Ammonia is less dense than air, making downward displacement of air the correct collection method.

q: A gas jar is known to be filled with ammonia if a moist red litmus paper placed at the mouth turns _____.
e: Ammonia is alkaline, so it turns moist red litmus paper blue.

q: Ammonia gas should not be dried by concentrated sulphuric acid because these compounds _____ with ammonia.
e: Acidic drying agents like concentrated sulphuric acid react with the basic ammonia gas.

q: Ammonia is extremely soluble in water, which is often demonstrated in the laboratory by the _____ experiment.
e: The Fountain experiment vividly demonstrates the high solubility of ammonia in water.

q: Liquid ammonia boils at _____ and freezes at -77.7℃.
e: The boiling point of liquid ammonia is -33.3℃.

q: Dense white fumes are observed when ammonia gas reacts with _____ gas to form solid ammonium chloride.
e: Ammonia reacts with hydrogen chloride gas to produce dense white fumes of solid ammonium chloride.

q: When ammonia is passed over heated copper(II) oxide, it reduces the copper(II) oxide to _____.
e: Ammonia acts as a reducing agent, reducing heated copper(II) oxide to metallic copper.

q: When excess ammonia reacts with chlorine, _____ is obtained.
e: With excess ammonia, the reaction with chlorine yields nitrogen gas and ammonium chloride.

q: If chlorine is in excess, the reaction with ammonia forms the explosive oily liquid substance, _____.
e: Excess chlorine reacting with ammonia produces highly explosive nitrogen trichloride ($NCl_3$).

q: Dry ammonia passed over sodium metal heated to red heat forms _____.
e: Heated sodium reacts with dry ammonia to form sodium amide (sodamide) and hydrogen gas.

q: Nitric acid is manufactured industrially by the _____ Process.
e: Nitric acid is produced via the Ammonia Oxidation Process (Ostwald process).

q: In the manufacture of nitric acid, the catalyst used in the oxidation of ammonia is a _____ gauze.
e: A Platinum-Rhodium (Pt-Rh) gauze catalyst is used to oxidise ammonia to nitrogen oxide.

q: Pure nitric acid is known as _____, which is Latin for 'strong water'.
e: Nitric acid is historically known as aqua fortis.

q: Nitric acid should be stored in _____ glass bottles because it decomposes when subject to heat or light.
e: Brown glass bottles protect nitric acid from light, preventing its decomposition.

q: Aqua regia is a mixture of 3 volumes concentrated hydrochloric acid and 1 volume concentrated _____.
e: Aqua regia is a 3:1 mixture of concentrated $HCl$ and concentrated $HNO_3$, capable of dissolving gold.
